subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should memoryFlush and preflight compaction remain synchronous with foreground session processing, move to a dedicated/background lane, or become preemptible when user messages arrive?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug is clear, but the fix changes scheduler and session-state ordering semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Dedicated maintenance lane
options.body: Move eligible memoryFlush and compaction work to a bounded maintenance lane with explicit ordering checkpoints for transcript reads and writes.

options.title: Preemptible foreground compaction
options.body: Keep the current lane but add maintainer-approved cancellation or preemption when foreground messages wait too long.

options.title: Timeout-only mitigation
options.body: Treat the existing shorter timeout and diagnostics as acceptable for now, leaving foreground messages blocked during active maintenance.

recommendation.title: Dedicated maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Move eligible memoryFlush and compaction work to a bounded maintenance lane with explicit ordering checkpoints for transcript reads and writes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this owner to the queued compaction wrapper and release area most likely to host the scheduler decision.
